portion_doctrine: Sales consulting + proposal design masterclass compilation. Three major operating systems distilled: (1) Three-Options Selling (Rana/Expert Project) - price-anchored close mechanism using high/middle/low tiers; (2) Strategic Proposal Architecture (Biz Chat/ProposalPhi) - proposal as plan anchor (promise-phases-logistics) not sales tool; (3) Pre-proposal Conversation Stack (HubSpot/Agency Training) - emotional foundation before document, objection clearing before cost reveal.
operating_rules: Never send proposal without pre-proposal 'brainstorm call' that qualifies problem and frames solution (prerequisite trust-build)
Proposal structure: Promise (what they want) + Phases (3-tier plan: Phase 1 detail-heavy, Phase 2-3 strategic outcomes) + Logistics + Investment + Benefits
Always offer 2 options minimum (cost-driven vs convenience-driven, or tiered high/middle/low); 3 options dilute decision
Lead with investment/fee early in proposal, never bury at end (anchors expectation, prevents sticker shock)
Brief = digestible; target 1-2 pages promise+plan, one page per phase breakdown. No linear 12-18 month roadmaps (too abstract)
Use cost/pricing as barrier to access (time access, service access, resource access); frame as money-to-understand-intent not price-gouging
Proposal must be summation of conversation already had, not Hail Mary cold send (retention suffers if proposal is primary sales tool)
Messaging: use partnership/collaboration language not vendor/supplier; echo client's own words back to show listening
Design principle: break up text-heavy sections with white space, imagery, section cover pages; reading is exhausting on eyes
Avoid customizing proposals for every client; template = 80% of outcome at 20% of effort. Adjust 20% for client context
Timing: Brainstorm call → book next call → send proposal between calls → use Loom video walkthrough to pre-answer objections → launch call closes
Competitive positioning: client has 3 real options: work with you, work with competitor, do nothing. Your job is trust+education not convincing
Price competition is loss condition; proposal closes on emotional conceptual buy-in already done pre-proposal, not price advantage
named_methods: Three Options Selling (Rana): High/Middle/Low tier structure so prospect always says yes to one of three options not binary yes/no
Expert Money Model (Expert Project): Promise (outcome) + 3 Foundations + Phases (revolutions) framework, service/resource/time access layers
Proposal = Plan (not proposal): Reframe word choice to shift from tactical proposal thinking to strategic plan thinking
Brainstorm call framework: Discover problem urgency, budget appetite, solution fit; condition prospect to think your way; prepare them for proposal
Loom proposal walkthrough: Video sent between brainstorm and launch call; prospect sees owner explain proposal; tracks if watched; pre-answers 80% of objections
Swiss-style design (368 agency): Minimal typography, clean grid, left-aligned text, lots of white space; good enough to skip heavy imagery
Cost vs Convenience matrix: Product A (productized/leveraged/cheaper) vs Product B (customized/hands-on/premium); access=differentiator
Phase-based outcome framing: Phase 1 = foundations+strategy (detailed, immediate action), Phase 2 = scale (recurring revenue focus), Phase 3 = efficiency (client becomes self-sufficient)
Section cover pages: Minimal graphic/color break between dense sections; gives eyes rest; reinforces brand color throughout
Case studies + imagery + explanation: Don't just show pretty work; explain brief+problem+solution+result so prospect imagines the working relationship
Notion as proposal template (Expert Project): Pseudo-flexible website; edit on-fly; live changes; maintains brand consistency; accessible to non-designers
Payment schedule + milestones: Set clear phases and payment dates; prevents waiting forever or scope creep; adds urgency to sign
numbers: 60-75% of prospects should be targeted at middle-tier option (not high, not low)
5-8 hours average time consultants spend on single proposal before acquiring client
If 4 proposals to close = 30+ hours unpaid before one client acquired (time math that justifies template investment)
80% of time prospect shows up to launch call with all info if Loom video walkthrough sent (objections pre-answered)
3 reasons people buy: Money (investment), Time (progress timeline), Energy (convenience/ease)
62% of sales professionals report spending 40 hours/week on proposals (entire work week waste)
Research shows single solution offering secures more deals than small/medium/large tiered menu
10K/month = focus of Phase 2; 500K annualized = Phase 3 outcome (for expert/consulting vertical)
Phase 1 should take 1-2 pages detail; Phases 2-3 strategic outcomes, 1 page total
Template investment = 80% of outcome at 20% of effort; customize final 20% per client
specific_tactics: Schedule brainstorm call (discovery) + close next call (launch), send proposal in between to give read time
In proposal cover letter: use client's exact language from brainstorm call to show you listened and understood
Promise section first paragraph must answer: Is this what you want? If no, stop reading (top-line filter)
Always explain 'why phase 1 detail matters: people lack strategy/structure; need it immediately to build confidence
When objections arise in launch call, restate the outcome they said they wanted, restate the reason they want it, ask 'should we move forward'
Use checkmarks, simple icons, blue accents to break up text; no need for heavy custom graphics if layout is clean
Include about/team section with photos: builds trust; people hire people, not logos
External link to terms/conditions on website, not embedded in proposal, keeps proposal length down and allows live updates
Add section for 'what we need from you at each stage' (feedback, files, decisions); manages expectations, prevents scope creep
End with soft send-off page that reinforces brand (no I in team type pun, contact info, value prop) not just budget
Pricing table: keep simple, readable, no unnecessary color; simplicity > decoration in financials
For discovery calls, ask: What's the main barrier preventing you from middle solution? = uncover objection, create corresponding low option
Loom script template: Hey [Name], here's what we do [phase 1 detail] then [phase 2 outcome] then [phase 3 outcome]; have any questions, bring to next call
Budget anchor early: When I asked about budget, you said around X, both options might work, we'll dial together on call
prompts: In proposal: 'This is the promise + why you want it. Does that resonate?' (yes=proceed, no=they've already disqualified)
Launch call close: 'Based on what you want to achieve, which of these three options feels most aligned?' (not 'what questions do you have')
Objection handling: 'I hear that concern about [cost/timeline/scope]. Here's why that's actually the strength of phase 1: [restate outcome]'
When client hesitates: 'I respect you want to know us better. Option 3 is designed exactly for that: month-to-month, low commitment, we'll earn your trust then upgrade'
Brainstorm close: 'Sounds like [problem] is the main thing stopping you. Let me send you a plan on how we'd tackle phase 1, read it, bring questions next call, okay?'
Proposal footer CTA: 'Have questions? Add them to the list and bring to [DATE] call. We'll align you with the right option.'
Post-Loom: 'I walked you through how phases stack. If you have any 'what if' questions, jot them down and we'll cover them together on the call'
Phase 2 framing: 'Once we've got phase 1 locked and you're hitting 10K/month, phase 2 is about making it consistent and predictable'
Rejected proposal follow-up: 'I totally understand it doesn't feel right. Sometimes it's timing, sometimes it's approach. What would make sense to revisit?'
Upsell in launch: 'I know you picked option 2, but just so you know, with option 3 you'd get [additional access]. Might be worth considering down the road.'
content_ideas: Design system for proposal templates (color palette, typography, icon set, section cover graphics); once built, reuse for years
Proposal writing masterclass: from brainstorm notes to proposal outline in 90 minutes using the promise-phases-logistics skeleton
Loom script templates for different verticals (agency, coaching, SaaS, product-based); client can adapt and send
Pre-proposal objection clearing framework: 'Here are the 7 most common objections in [vertical], here's how we pre-answer them in brainstorm'
Case study package format: [Client Logo] + [Problem Statement] + [Our Approach] + [Results/Outcome]; template that works across industries
Proposal design audit checklist: 10-point rapid assessment (white space, typography, CTA clarity, image:text ratio, phase structure readability)
Cost-vs-Convenience positioning guide: how to build credible Product A (productized) and Product B (hands-on) without looking cheap
Phase-outcome language bank: 250+ outcome statements indexed by vertical (SaaS launch, brand refresh, content strategy, hiring system, etc.)
Brainstorm call recording guide: what to listen for, how to turn notes into proposal content, templates for translating discovery into plan
Timeline visualization best practices: Gantt-style timelines lose to milestone-outcome timelines; examples of what lands
Team photo strategy: why solo founders win more than headshot collages; production notes for non-designer entrepreneurs
Section cover page generator: minimalist template (3 color, 1 graphic, headline); swap in client name and phase number
gates: Before sending proposal: Brainstorm call must be completed AND prospect must have indicated budget appetite AND solution fit confirmed
Proposal document: Must have explicit promise statement in first paragraph (if prospect doesn't see their want in first 100 words, they stop reading)
Phase 1 detail: Must include specific first steps (offer, lead system, sales sequence, etc.) not abstract roadmap; if too vague, credibility fails
Investment section: Must appear before benefits/logistics (anchor early); must frame as access-to-time/services/resources not just hourly
CTA: Must be linked to next scheduled call (not vague 'let us know'); must assume yes not ask for yes
Design gate: One image per two pages minimum (text fatigue risk); no more than 2 colors beyond brand black/white (overcomplication kills trust)
Customization gate: If more than 30% of proposal is unique to client, your template is wrong (cost/time blows up)
Launch call prerequisite: Prospect must have read proposal and written down questions (Loom tracking confirms); no re-pitching allowed
contradictions: Tension: Three options said to prevent decision paralysis but also '3 is a crowd'; resolution: 3rd is 'future upgrade path after client becomes user', not equal tier
Tension: Proposal is 'evergreen architecture' (reusable) but also must 'show you listened' (customized); resolution: template 80%, customize promise/client-specific examples 20%
Tension: 'Proposal doesn't sell, conversation does' vs 'proposal is your primary tool'; resolution: proposal seals (rationalizes decision already made emotionally), not initiates
Tension: Detailed Phase 1 needed vs brief proposal (1-2 pages); resolution: phase 1 gets 1 page detail, phases 2-3 are outcome-only, logistics/benefits compressed
Tension: Use simple design vs stand out with photography; resolution: both work; Swiss minimalism works if text/layout is clean, photo-heavy works if photos are metaphorical not literal
Tension: Budget hidden until late vs investment early; resolution: investment section early (sets expectation), granular pricing/terms can be summary with terms linked externally

weird_gold: The $335,000 hammer story (consultant invoices for 2 mins work = 35 years of knowledge about WHERE to tap): ROI of consulting is insight speed not labor hours; applies to small proposal tweaks that shift client decision by 200K
Notion used as 'pseudo-flexible website' not just document = full live-edit on brainstorm call, change words mid-meeting, show prospect the real-time fluidity
Three options always close to 'yes' because even if they hate option 1 and 2, they can say yes to option 3 as 'test relationship'; removes binary rejection
Loom tracking shows if prospect watched video = Intel for launch call (if unwatched, they're not serious; if watched, 80% of objections pre-cleared)

Phase 1 detail MUST be granular (offer building, lead system, sales sequence) because people lacking strategy need immediate structure; phases 2-3 stay outcome-only (dynamic environment doesn't support linear)
Proposal worth 3-5 hours design investment upfront (template + graphics) because it pays for itself in first 4-5 proposals (80% outcome at 20% effort)
Section cover pages with brand color and minimal graphic = visual rest (so text doesn't fatigue) AND reinforces brand in subconscious (color on every page)
External link to terms/conditions (not embedded) = short proposal + live-update ability + no PDF versioning chaos
End proposal with BRAND REINFORCEMENT not budget (last image/page in prospect's mind = brand, not cost) = psychological recency bias hack
